newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU cartel office talks seen fading - Van Miert.
newsitem.headline: EU cartel office talks seen fading - Van Miert.

text.p: European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert said on Monday he thought a German proposal for a European independent cartel office would be short lived because there was no need for it.
The German Federal Cartel Office recently launched a campaign for the creation of a European competition authority that would be separated from the EU's institutions.
But Van Miert said the Commission would fight the proposal tooth and nail as it saw no need for such a body.
"I can say that it looks as if this idea is not going to be pursued," he told a seminar on competition policy organised by a Brussels-based think-tank, Centre for European Policy Studies.

Van Miert questioned whether a "hypothetical" cartel office would be independent from political interference, saying that even those who advocated the idea regularly tried to pressure the Commission on cases of their own interests -- an apparent nod to the EU-German fight over Volkswagen subsidies.
The head of Italy's anti-trust authority, Giuliano Amato, was previously reported to have supported the German move.
But Van Miert said Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi had ensured him in a recent meeting in Rome that the plan did not have Italy's backing.

He added "even in Germany, some now wondered" whether there was a need to discuss the issue at the EU's inter-governmental conference started earlier this year to revise the bloc's institutions ahead of enlargement to eastern Europe.
